features.text: The patient has pain in the big toe that is throbbing and occasionally sharp, especially when moving or walking.
The patient's big toe is red and warm to touch.
The patient has been experiencing pain in the big toe for about two weeks, with increased pain in the last week.
The patient avoids walking on the big toe and walks on the heel instead.
The patient experiences pain at night when the sheets touch the toe or when rolling over in bed.
The patient takes ibuprofen twice a day, but it does not seem to help.
The patient does not ride bikes and prefers running.
The patient does not wear clips on the bike and usually wears regular shoes or flip-flops.
The patient does not recall any injury related to the onset of the symptoms.
The patient does not have a history of stomach problems.
The patient enjoys spicy Mexican food.
The patient prefers to continue working and doing regular activities rather than taking time off.
The patient's big toe has limited range of motion, with pain during plantar flexion and movement.
The patient has a bone spur on the top of the big toe joint.
The patient has lost a significant amount of cartilage in the big toe joint.
The patient has arthritis in the big toe joint, referred to as hallux rigidus.
